checks: For bounded Borel A each phase mass is a measurable finite sum of fiber volumes by Tonelli. For each z the change of variable x=z+t integrates over its half-open cell, and the disjoint cells cover the full base space. Applying Tonelli to the continuous coordinates gives ambient volume. With d=0 the same argument integrates an indicator.

At every zero-mass phase the captured mass is also zero, so the product M_t(C)p_t(H) is exactly M_t(C∩H) for all phases. The integral of the nonnegative weight equals the positive full ambient volume of C.

When M_0(C)>0 all p_0(H_j) are actual ratios. Pull each out of the integral, apply the identity to each H_j, and take the finite real combination. The original §1 uses exactly this weighting and supplies no conclusion at phase zero by itself.

overlap.comparison: This accepted result gives a fixed-coset discrepancy estimate for convex sets and caps, measured in units of cell radius. It does not integrate all translations or state the weighted ratio and signed identity for the original phase.

readability: The averaging measure is M_t(C) times Lebesgue measure on the phase cell.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The disjoint unit-cell decomposition gives the exact weighted phase identity and its finite signed combination, including zero-mass phases.
